'''Kálmán Géza Vánky''' (15 June 1930 – 18 October 2021) was a Hungarian [[mycology|mycologist]] with Swedish and Hungarian citizenship, who lived in Germany. He was considered to be the worldwide authority on the subject of [[smut (fungus)|smut fungi]] and has dominated the taxonomic study of [[Ustilaginomycetes]] for at least the past four decades.<ref name="DAFF"/>

==Early life and education==
Vánky was born in {{lang|ro|[[Odorheiu Secuiesc]]}} ({{lang|hu|Székelyudvarhely}}), [[Romania]] on 15 June 1930. He attended the Bethlen János Reformed School and, after it closed in 1945, the United Grammar School in Odorhei until 1949. He then began his studies at the [[Babeș-Bolyai University|University of Cluj]] (Kolozsvár) in [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]] but completed his degree in biology at the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1953.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}

==Early career==
Between 1953 and 1957 Vánky worked as a researcher with Professor [[Traian Săvulescu]] at the Department of Phytopathology of the Agricultural Research Institute, Bucharest, Romania, where he began studying [[smut (fungus)|smut fungi]]. However – as he always wanted to be a physician – in 1957 he left Bucharest for the Faculty of Medicine, [[Tîrgu-Mureş]] (Marosvásárhely), Romania, where he obtained his [[Doctor of Medicine|MD]] in 1961. From 1961 until 1964 he worked as a [[general practitioner]] in [[Odorhei]] (Székelyudvarhely), then, until 1969, he worked as a [[Balneotherapy|balneologist]] in [[Borszék]] but continued studying and collecting smut fungi.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}

In 1969 he left [[Nicolae Ceaușescu|Ceauşescu]]'s Romania and settled in Sweden, where he obtained the Swedish MD and worked as a family physician in [[Gagnef]] village. He continued to pursue and personally fund his research in the field of smut fungus taxonomy and obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in taxonomic botany at [[Uppsala University]] in 1985 (under supervision of Prof. Jan Axel Nannfeldt).{{citation needed|date=March 2015}} His doctoral thesis, ''Carpathian Ustilaginales'', was published in the [[academic journal]] ''[[Symbolae Botanicae Upsalienses]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Carpathian Ustilaginales| journal=Symbolae Botanicae |year=1985 |first=Kalman |last=Vánky |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=1–309}}</ref>

==Professional mycology==
In 1986 Vánky obtained a one-year [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG-scholarship]] in Germany and worked in the field of smut fungus [[taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]] at the [[University of Tübingen]], Institute of Botany, Department of Special Botany and Mycology (with Prof. Franz Oberwinkler). As the scholarship was extended successively, he decided to focus his career on mycology rather than medicine. <!-- because he thought he was much better (or rather the best) as an expert of smut fungi. However he never ceased to miss his earlier activity, which was a sort of selfless aid to people. --> He continued to work at the university until his retirement in 1995.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}

==Death==
Vánky died on 18 October 2021, at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s11557-022-01801-4 | title=Obituary for Kálmán Vánky (1930–2021) | year=2022 | last1=Shivas | first1=Roger | last2=McTaggart | first2=Alistair | last3=Begerow | first3=Dominik | last4=Denchev | first4=Cvetomir M. | last5=Denchev | first5=Teodor T. | last6=Kemler | first6=Martin | last7=Kruse | first7=Julia | last8=Lutz | first8=Matthias | last9=Piątek | first9=Marcin | last10=Piepenbring | first10=Meike | last11=Thines | first11=Marco | journal=Mycological Progress | volume=21 | issue=5 | s2cid=248487641 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Obituary for Kálmán Vánky (1930–2021) |journal=Mycological Progress |date=30 April 2022|doi=10.1007/s11557-022-01801-4 |last1=Shivas |first1=Roger |last2=McTaggart |first2=Alistair |last3=Begerow |first3=Dominik |last4=Denchev |first4=Cvetomir M. |last5=Denchev |first5=Teodor T. |last6=Kemler |first6=Martin |last7=Kruse |first7=Julia |last8=Lutz |first8=Matthias |last9=Piątek |first9=Marcin |last10=Piepenbring |first10=Meike |last11=Thines |first11=Marco |volume=21 |issue=5 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Publications==
By 2014 Vánky had published 232 scientific papers and 10 books on smut fungi. His monograph ''Smut Fungi of the World'', published in 2012 by ([[American Phytopathological Society|APS Press]]) was described as “a culmination of more than 50 years of dedicated work and passion for smut fungi.”<ref>{{cite book
|first=Kalman |last=Vánky |title=Smut Fungi of the World |year=2012 |publisher=[[American Phytopathological Society|APS Press]]|isbn=9780890543986 |pages=1480}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/102/09/1316.pdf |title=Smut Fungi of the World |department=Book Reviews |first=N.D. |last=Sharma |journal=Current Science |volume=102 |issue=9 |pages=1316–1318 |date=10 May 2012}}</ref> The nearly 1500 page monograph has been described as the "Holy Book of Smut Fungi", because it comprises the description of the 1700 known species with their synonyms, important literature, their host plants and over 3.500 illustrations of which 650 are the author's drawings of smutted plants.<ref>{{cite journal |department=Book reviews |title=Smut Fungi of the World |journal=Fungal Diversity |date=15 March 2013 |volume=59 |issue=1 | pages=179–197|doi=10.1007/s13225-013-0221-1 |last1 = Karunarathna|first1 = Samantha C.|last2=Daranagama |first2=Anupama |last3=Wulandari |first3=Nilam Fadmaulidha |last4=Luangharn |first4=Thatsanee |last5=Jayawardena |first5=M. M. Ruvishika S. |last6=Herath |first6=P. H. M. Anushika K. |last7=Dissanayake |first7=Asha Janadaree |last8=Abeysinghe |first8=Gayan Dakshitha |last9=Senanayake |first9=I. C. |last10=Hongsanan |first10=Sinang |last11=Hyde |first11=Kevin D. |s2cid=4747529 }}</ref>

The third edition of his ''Illustrated Genera of Smut Fungi'' was published in 2013. In this edition, 104 recognized genera of smut fungi are presented, described and illustrated, compared to the second edition, in which 77 genera are identified.<ref>{{cite book |url=http://www.apsnet.org/apsstore/shopapspress/Pages/44280.aspx |title=Illustrated Genera of Smut Fungi |first=Kalman |last=Vánky |publisher=[[American Phytopathological Society|APS Press]] |year=2013 |edition=3 |isbn=9780890544280 |pages=288 |access-date=20 March 2015 |archive-date=2 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402112035/http://www.apsnet.org/apsstore/shopapspress/Pages/44280.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Collections==
Both before and after retirement, Vánky travelled widely, collecting and investigating smut fungi in about 55 countries all over the world.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kalman-vanky.de/collecting-trips-1.html |first=Kalman |last=Vánky |title=Collecting Trips |access-date=19 March 2015}}</ref> The collecting trips were very often combined with national or international workshops, conferences or congresses in the field of mycology, where he was lecturer or speaker. Between 1989 and 2009 his German wife, Christine, helped him in collecting and taking photos of smutted plants.<ref name="DAFF">{{cite web |url=http://collections.daff.qld.gov.au/web/key/smutfungi/Media/Html/history.html |title=Smut fungi of Australia |publisher=Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, [[Queensland]] Government |access-date=19 March 2015}}</ref>

Over 60 years Vánky amassed the largest smut fungus collection in the world, ''Herbarium Ustilaginales Vánky (HUV)'', containing over 22,000 samples. In August 2013 it was relocated to the [[Queensland Plant Pathology Herbarium]], [[Brisbane]], Australia (‘BRIP’), and placed at the disposal of the mycological community.<ref>{{cite web |title=Australia gets world's biggest smut collection |url=http://www.pbcrc.com.au/sites/default/files/managed/file-attach/media/PBCRC%20media%20release%20-%20Australia%20gets%20worlds%20biggest%20smut%20collection%20-%20November%202013_0.pdf |date=20 November 2013 |publisher=Plant Biosecurity Cooperative Research Centre |location=Brisbane |access-date=20 March 2015 |archive-date=3 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215317/http://www.pbcrc.com.au/sites/default/files/managed/file-attach/media/PBCRC%20media%20release%20-%20Australia%20gets%20worlds%20biggest%20smut%20collection%20-%20November%202013_0.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Vánky lectured in Hungary. He donated a complete set (no. 1–1350) of his Smut fungus [[exsiccata]] series ''Ustilaginales exsiccata'', issued between 1975 and 2009,<ref name="Triebel & Scholz 2001-2024">Triebel, D. & Scholz, P. 2001–2024 ''IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae''. – Botanische Staatssammlung München: http://indexs.botanischestaatssammlung.de. – München, Germany.</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ustilaginales exsiccata: IndExs ExsiccataID=697799622 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=697799622 |access-date=22 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ustilaginales exsiccata: IndExs ExsiccataID=623645841 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=623645841 |access-date=22 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ustilaginales exsiccata: IndExs ExsiccataID=558303832 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=558303832 |access-date=22 September 2024}}</ref> and several hundreds of duplicates, between them numerous precious [[isotype (biology)|isotypes]], as well as all of his smut fungus books and publications to the [[Hungarian Natural History Museum]].{{when|date=March 2015}}{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}

==Interviews, awards and honours==
In June 1996 an interview with Vánky entitled "{{lang|hu|Egy világutazó székely füvész}}" (A world travelling Székely botanist) was published in ''{{lang|hu|A Természet Világa}}'' (The World of Nature).<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://arago.elte.hu/sites/default/files/VankyInterju_TV-1996.pdf |title=Egy világutazó székely füvész|language=hu|trans-title=A world travelling Székely botanist| first=Gabor|last=Horvath | date=June 1996 |journal=A Természet Világa | volume=127 |issue=12 |pages=250–254}}</ref> The Romanian journal ''{{lang|ro|Moeszia - Erdélyi Gombász}}'' ''(Transylvanian Mycologist)'' published two interviews and a laudation on the Székely-Hungarian scientist.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Zsigmond |last=Győző |journal=Moeszia |url=http://www.gombasz.ro/letoltes/moeszia_7-8.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402095158/http://www.gombasz.ro/letoltes/moeszia_7-8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 April 2015 |language=hu |title=Világutazó székely-magyar tudós – Két interjú Vánky Kálmánnal |trans-title=Two Interviews with the Székely-Hungarian Scientist Kálmán Vánky |volume=7–8 |pages=66–72 |year=2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=Zsigmond |last=Győző |journal=Moeszia |url=http://www.gombasz.ro/letoltes/moeszia_7-8.pdf |language=hu |title=Vánky Kálmán laudációja |trans-title=Laudation of Kálmán Vánky |volume=7–8 |page=73 |year=2013 |access-date=20 March 2015 |archive-date=2 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402095158/http://www.gombasz.ro/letoltes/moeszia_7-8.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
In 2012 he was awarded the "Pázmány Dénes Award" of the 'Kálmán László Mycological Society', Transylvania (Romania).{{citation needed|date=March 2015}} and in 2014 awarded with "Arany János medal" of the 'Hungarian Academy of Science'.

Two new genera of smut fungi, ''[[Vankya]]''<ref>{{cite journal |url=http://en.journals.sid.ir/ViewPaper.aspx?ID=44060 |journal=Rostaniha |year=2000 |volume=1 |number=1–4 |pages=151 161| title=Vankya, a new genus of smut fungi |first=J. |last=Ershad}}</ref> and ''Kalmanago'',<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Mycobiota |year=2020 |volume=10 |pages=21–37| title=''Kalmanago'' gen. nov. (''Microbotryaceae'') on ''Commelina'' and ''Tinantia (Commelinaceae)''. |first1=T.T. |last1=Denchev |last2=Denchev |last3=Kemler |first3=M. |last4=Begerow |first4=D. |doi=10.12664/mycobiota.2020.10.03 |doi-access=free }}</ref> was named in his honour and several new species ''Orphanomyces vankyi'' Savile (1974),<ref>{{cite journal |first=D.B.O. |last=Savile |journal=Canadian Journal of Botany |title=Orphanomyces, a new genus of cypericolous smuts |volume=52
|issue=2 |pages=341–343 |year=1974 |doi=10.1139/b74-045}}</ref> ''Anthracoidea vankyi'' Nannfeldt (1977),<ref>{{cite journal |last=Nannfeldt |first=J.A. |year=1977 |title=The species of Anthracoidea (Ustilaginales)on Carex subgen. Vignea with special regard to the Nordic species |journal=Botaniska Notiser |volume=130 |issue=4 |pages=351–375}}</ref> ''Uromyces vankyorum'' R. Berndt (2002),<ref>{{cite journal
|last=Berndt |first=R. |year=2002 |title=Uromyces vankyorum spec. nov. and Uromyces atriplicis, putative vicariant rust species of Patagonian and Australian semi-desert biomes |journal=Mycological Progress |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=179–186 |doi=10.1007/s11557-006-0017-8|s2cid=27175590 }}</ref> ''Tilletia vankyi'' Carris & Castlebury (2007)<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Mycol. Res. |date=December 2007 |volume=111 |issue=12 |pages=1386–98 |title=Tilletia vankyi, a new species of reticulate-spored bunt fungus with non-conjugating basidiospores infecting species of Festuca and Lolium |last1=Carris |first1=LM1 |last2=Castlebury |first2=LA |last3=Huang |first3=G |last4=Alderman |first4=SC |last5=Luo |first5=J |last6=Bao |first6=X |doi=10.1016/j.mycres.2007.09.008 |pmid=18023991 |url=https://naldc-legacy.nal.usda.gov/naldc/download.xhtml?id=13487&content=PDF |url-access=subscription }}{{dead link|date=June 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and ''Macalpinomyces vankyi'' Y.M. Li, R.G. Shivas, McTaggart & L. Cai (2017)<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Mycologia |date=2017 |volume=109 |pages=408–421 |title=Ten new species of ''Macalpinomyces'' on ''Eriachne'' in northern Australia. |last1=Li |first1=Y.M. |last2=Shivas |first2=R.G. |last3=McTaggart |last4=Cai |first4=L |issue=3 |doi=10.1080/00275514.2017.1330026 |pmid=28636469 |hdl=2263/63261 |s2cid=22108236 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> were named for him.

He became honorary member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in the Biological Sciences section in 2001.{{citation needed|date=March 2015}}
